Claim 1 (Currently amended): A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising one or more logic circuits __including a hardware entropy source, a function processor, a pseudorandom number generator, and a cryptographic processor,__ configured to at least: receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from __the__ hardware source; apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seed __the__ pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number __wherein the function processor applies a cryptographic hash function to combine the plurality of independent first entropy values__.

Claim 2 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number __using an Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encryption algorithm__.

Claim 3 (Currently amended): The [[systemof]] __system of__ claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to at least: implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key __wherein the key-agreement protocol is an Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) protocol__.

Claim 4 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator __wherein the ring oscillator operates at a frequency that varies based on manufacturing process variations and environmental conditions__.

Claim 5 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source __wherein the plurality of independent first entropy values are temporally separated samples from the single hardware source__.

Claim 6 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source __comprises__ [[is]] a plurality of independent hardware sources, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

Claim 7 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function __wherein the permutation function is a cryptographic permutation that provides avalanche effect__.

Claim 8 (Currently amended): The system of claim 7, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to: divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values; apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value __wherein each group contains a predetermined number of bits and the permutation function processes each group independently__.

Claim 9 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function __wherein the hash function is a SHA-256 cryptographic hash function__.

Claim 10 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer __wherein the bit-mixer performs exclusive-OR operations and bit rotations on the plurality of independent first entropy values__.

Claim 11 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value __wherein the selection is based on a quality assessment of each entropy value__.

Claim 12 (Currently amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value __wherein the secret key is stored in tamper-resistant memory__.

Claim 13 (Currently amended): A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising: receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value __wherein the function is a cryptographic hash function__; seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

Claim 14 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number __using an Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encryption algorithm__.

Claim 15 (Original): The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least: implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

Claim 16 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator __wherein the ring oscillator operates at a frequency that varies based on manufacturing process variations and environmental conditions__.

Claim 17 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source __wherein the plurality of independent first entropy values are temporally separated samples from the single hardware source__.

Claim 18 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source __comprises__ [[is]] a plurality of independent hardware sources, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

Claim 19 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function __wherein the permutation function is a cryptographic permutation that provides avalanche effect__.

Claim 20 (Currently amended): The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes: dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values; applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value __wherein each group contains a predetermined number of bits and the permutation function processes each group independently__.

Claim 21 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function __wherein the hash function is a SHA-256 cryptographic hash function__.

Claim 22 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer __wherein the bit-mixer performs exclusive-OR operations and bit rotations on the plurality of independent first entropy values__.

Claim 23 (Currently amended): The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value __wherein the selection is based on a quality assessment of each entropy value__.

Claim 24 (Original): The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
